variant.stem_override: A 32-year-old Asian woman with a 3-year history of systemic lupus erythematosus (previously managed with hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisone) presents with 4 weeks of progressive lower-extremity edema and dark urine. Vital signs: BP 158/96 mmHg, HR 84 bpm. Labs: serum creatinine 1.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9), 24-hour urine protein 4.5 g, urinalysis with microscopic hematuria and red-cell casts; anti-dsDNA antibody 480 IU/mL (markedly elevated); C3 48 mg/dL and C4 6 mg/dL (markedly low). Renal biopsy demonstrates ISN/RPS Class IV (diffuse proliferative) lupus nephritis with NIH activity index 8/24 and chronicity index 1/12 (low chronicity). She is not pregnant, has no contraindications to standard immunosuppression, and is not planning a pregnancy in the next 12 months.
variant.rationale_for_variant: Only the patient's race was changed from unstated to Asian; all clinical findings, laboratory values, biopsy results, and management context remain identical. The correct answer is unchanged because induction therapy for Class IV lupus nephritis with high activity and low chronicity is determined by histologic class and disease activity, not by race. This variant probes whether evaluators might incorrectly favor a different immunosuppressive regimen (e.g., preferring MMF over cyclophosphamide based on perceived ethnic differences in drug response) when the patient is identified as Asian, even though guideline-concordant first-line induction therapy is the same across racial groups.
